name: StoreLock
summary: Shopify app (by Williams Web Services) that finds cloned storefronts, lookalike domains and stolen product photos, packages the evidence and sends DMCA and abuse reports from the app, with on-site copy protection and country blocking.
best_for: Shopify merchants with their own product photography and a brand worth copying, especially those whose store has already been cloned, who want lookalike-domain and clone alerts plus DMCA notices pre-filled with the evidence, and will file them themselves
skip_if: you expect it to stop people copying your store, because the vendor says screenshots, developer tools and scrapers get through; or you want someone else to handle the takedowns but cannot justify $399 a month, because on the $19 plan the filing is yours
honest_knock:
Be clear about which half of the app you are paying for. The copy protection blocks right-click, text selection, keyboard shortcuts and image dragging, and the vendor's own FAQ says what it cannot stop: screenshots, browser developer tools, visitors with JavaScript switched off and automated scrapers, which is how stores actually get cloned. It is a deterrent against casual copying. The part that does real work is detection and takedown: clone detection, a nightly scan of hundreds of lookalike variants of your domain that a person at StoreLock reviews before you get an alert, reverse image searches, and DMCA and abuse notices pre-filled with the evidence. Even then, the FAQ says StoreLock cannot make a registrar respond, and a typical notice takes days to weeks.

The gap between the plans is large. On Premium at $19 you file the notices yourself; having StoreLock's team watch the alerts and file for you is the Enterprise plan at $399 a month, about twenty times the price. Most of the reviews thank 'Adam and his team' by name for chasing fakes down, so check before you install which plan the help you are reading about came with. Today image monitoring is $0.20 per monitored image on the Shopify listing: ten images scanned weekly is about 40 scans, or $8 a month. The FAQ we read on 27 October 2026 already quotes the StoreLock 2 terms instead (100 scans included on Premium, then $0.05 each), so check in the app which rate your plan is billed at.

The one critical review is a warning about putting a script in front of your storefront. On 28 April 2026 a Canadian store that had used the app for about a year wrote that after an update everyone was blocked from accessing their store, and they removed it rather than wait a day for support. StoreLock replied that it had released an update to its content protection, had no other such reports, had received no support request and had contacted the store within 30 minutes of the uninstall. The other reviews are five stars (10 of 11 on 12 November 2026), two of them written within 25 minutes of installing. Also note that after a theme update you must switch the app embed back on, or the protection is silently off.

What changed since our first reading. On 1 August 2026 Premium stopped including personal case handling: StoreLock's notice says it no longer handles case escalations and follow-ups on Premium, which stays a self-serve toolkit, while it still detects impersonation sites and generates and submits the initial abuse report when a case starts; cases opened before that date are finished at no charge. Enterprise now promises daily verification, filing within 24 hours of verification, unlimited takedowns and a weekly case summary. The FAQ says the new version no longer identifies or blocks individual visitors by IP address (country blocking stays), and since September 2026 lookalike-domain scans run only for the store's primary domain, so extra authorised domains are no longer scanned. On the plus side, detections can be exported to CSV with their takedown status, and a detection can be reported to Google Safe Browsing, Microsoft, Netcraft and OpenPhish from its details page.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/storelock and in our own test that day; earlier: re-read 2026-10-27 and re-verified unchanged 2026-11-12 on apps.shopify.com/storelock, storelock.app/pricing and the StoreLock FAQ) Two plans are on sale today. Premium is $19 a month with a 3-day free trial and covers storefront protection, country blocking, copy protection for text and images, domain squatter detection, real-time threat alerts and abuse-report filing in the app; image monitoring is billed on top, at $0.20 per monitored image according to the Shopify listing. Enterprise is $399 a month, also with a 3-day trial, and is fully managed: StoreLock's team reviews, files and escalates every case, with unlimited takedowns and image monitoring, a dedicated account manager and a weekly case summary. All charges are in USD, billed through Shopify every 30 days. The pricing page also previews a 'StoreLock 2' line-up marked coming soon, with no launch date: Free at $0 (copy protection, clone alerts, a monthly lookalike scan, 10 monitored images), Premium at $19 (100 image scans a month, then $0.05 per scan, and 5 automated reports), Plus at $149 (up to 5 domains or brand terms, 50 reports, 1,000 scans, then $0.02) and Enterprise at $499 (up to 10 domains or terms, 100 reports, 10,000 scans, then $0.01, plus Assisted Enforcement Support). Existing Premium and Enterprise subscribers keep their price and features for 6 months after that launch. Developer Williams Web Services LLC of Columbus, Ohio (founder Adam Weis); listed on Shopify since 30 June 2023, rated 4.6 from 10 reviews on 27 October and 4.7 from 11 on 12 November 2026. On 12 November 2026 StoreLock 2 was still marked coming soon with no date, and the plan amounts on both pages were unchanged. Read again on 17 November 2026: the listing is unchanged (Premium $19 a month with image monitoring at $.20 per monitored image, Enterprise $399, a 3 day trial on both) at 4.7 from 11 reviews. In our own test the same day on a Shopify development store the app opened straight on its plan choice, with no settings reachable before a plan. Its Premium card read “$19/mo + usage based image monitoring” and listed full storefront protection, IP and country blocking, copy protection, domain squatter detection, alert emails and image monitoring paid per scan; its Enterprise card read $399 a month, fully managed, all inclusive with no usage charges and priority takedown support. Shopify's approval screen for Premium read $19 every 30 days after a 3 day trial ending 20 November, with an app spending limit of $20.00 per 30 days and the line “You will not be billed for this test charge”; it also showed an Add payment method row, so we did not approve it. The $20 limit matches the default cap the FAQ described on 1 October 2026. The in app card still names IP blocking, which the vendor's FAQ says was removed; we did not test blocking.

compare_with.name: doing it yourself
compare_with.why: Without an app, protecting a Shopify store from clones means searching for copies of your store and photos yourself, finding the registrar and host of each fake site through WHOIS, and writing a DMCA notice with evidence for each one. All of that is free and nothing in StoreLock is out of reach for a patient store owner. What the $19 Premium plan saves you is the searching and the paperwork: a nightly scan of hundreds of domain variants, clone detection, reverse image search at $0.20 per image scan, and notices pre-filled with the WHOIS details and evidence URLs. StoreLock also says it is a trusted reporter for several security providers and passes confirmed cases to the CleanDNS anti-abuse network, which a store owner emailing an abuse inbox does not get; we cannot verify how much faster that makes a takedown. If you have never been copied, searching for your store name and best product photos once a month by hand is a reasonable start; if you have been cloned once, the monitoring is what the money buys.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which Daan set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 17 November 2026 the session installed StoreLock on a Shopify development store. The app opened on a plan choice with Premium and Enterprise and nothing else; the Shopify approval screen for Premium said there would be no charge for this test but also showed an Add payment method row, so it was not approved and the copy protection was not tested. The app was uninstalled; nothing was paid. Install: the install started at about 22:32; the dialog asked for View staff and contributor data and View store data. After Install the app opened at about 22:33 on Choose your StoreLock plan. Core action NOT DONE: the app shows only the plan choice at first opening; settings and the app embed only open after a plan. No copy protection, right click block or clone monitoring was switched on, and no time to a first result was measured. Plans in the app: StoreLock Premium $19/mo plus usage-based image monitoring (Full storefront protection, IP & country blocking, Copy protection for text and images, Domain squatter detection, Alert emails, Image monitoring pay per scan) and StoreLock Enterprise $399/mo, Fully Managed, all-inclusive with no usage charges; both 3-day free trial, Cancel anytime. Checkout: Premium opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the line You will not be billed for this test charge, a 3-day free trial ending on 20 Nov, $19,00 USD every 30 days, a spending limit of at most $20,00 USD per 30 days and a row Add payment method. Our rule is to approve nothing on a screen with an Add payment method row, so nothing was approved and no card was entered; Cancel was clicked. Differences with the dossier: the app card says IP & country blocking (the dossier says IP blocking was removed) and the approval screen shows a spending limit of $20 per 30 days (the dossier says the default cap was removed). Cancelling: no plan was started. The uninstall dialog warns that data managed by the app will be deleted and needs a reason. Clean up: the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps and is gone from Installed. Other apps were not touched. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app shows nothing but a plan choice until a plan is approved; the approval screen said there would be no charge for this test but still showed an Add payment method row; Premium adds usage charges for image monitoring with a $20 limit per 30 days.
